connections.observation: ὄψον (s001) appears first as absence, then as simple provision, then as luxury; τραγήματα (s002) shift from simple (figs, chickpeas) to conventional items; κλῖναι and τράπεζαι (s009) move from Glaucon's demand to Socrates' catalogue. Held together, these recurrences show the section's repeated pattern: Glaucon names a lack or demand, Socrates responds first simply, then incorporates the luxury version into the expanded city's inventory.

Glaucon's ὑῶν πόλιν (s003) uses the genitive of pigs to characterize the city; ἐχόρταζες versus ἑστιωμένους (s017) opposes animal feeding to human feasting. When the luxurious city requires συβωτῶν (s003), swineherds enter not to feed citizens as pigs but to supply the meat luxury demands, reversing the trajectory of Glaucon's insult.

ὑγίεια/ὑγιής/ὑγιεινή (s004) characterize the simple city and its citizens' life; φλεγμαίνουσαν and ἀληθινή (s005) name the two cities as diseased and true. The configuration makes visible that health moves from a condition enjoyed by persons (μετὰ ὑγιείας) to a quality predicated of the city itself (ὑγιής, ὑγιεινή), while the luxurious alternative receives a medical term for inflammation.

ἱκανός (s006) shifts from sufficient to insufficient as the city expands; τὸ ἀναγκαῖον (s007) marks the boundary that is transgressed; ἀποτμητέον and ὑπερβάντες (s015) express territorial cutting and limit-crossing. Together these show sufficiency yielding to insufficiency through the stepping-beyond (ὑπερβάντες) of necessity's limit (ὅρον), which then requires cutting into (ἀποτμητέον) neighbours' territory.

The simple city lives ἐν εἰρήνῃ (s008); the section concludes with πολέμου γένεσιν ηὑρήκαμεν and the evils war brings ἰδίᾳ καὶ δημοσίᾳ (s016). The configuration shows peace as the condition of the healthy city's life and war's genesis as what has been discovered (ηὑρήκαμεν) by the inquiry's movement, framing the section's trajectory from one condition to its opposite origin.

δέω/προσδέω (s010) accumulates five times at 373c; luxury goods (s012), artistic occupations (s013), and service workers (s014) appear in dense catalogues at 373a–c. The repeated expression of need (δεησόμεθα, δεήσει, προσδεήσει) accompanied by proliferating lists makes visible that luxury generates need through multiplication of items and roles rather than through scarcity of existing goods.

The simple city's citizens παραδώσουσιν the same life to their offspring (s011) and live ἐν εἰρήνῃ (s008); the section ends with war's genesis. Held together, intergenerational transmission (παραδώσουσιν) of an unchanging life in peace gives way to a discovered origin (γένεσιν) of war, showing transmission replaced by genesis as the section's governing temporal figure.

σκοπέω (s018) appears twice as Socrates redefines the scope from examining one city to examining a luxurious city as well; this redefinition is justified by the possibility that they might κατίδοιμεν where δικαιοσύνην and ἀδικίαν grow in cities (s019). The shift in what is being examined (σκοποῦμεν) is tied to the visual verb κατίδοιμεν, making the expansion of the inquiry's object a condition for seeing its original goal.

ὄψον (s001) recurs from absence to simple provision to luxury catalogue; δέω (s010) concentrates at the point where service workers are enumerated; ὀψοποιῶν and μαγείρων (s014) appear among those workers. The recurrence shows ὄψον moving from a single disputed item to the generator of specialist roles (ὀψοποιῶν, μαγείρων) whose necessity is repeatedly asserted (δεήσει, προσδεησόμεθα).

The healthy city is characterized by ὑγίεια (s004); war's γένεσιν (s016) is identified as the source of κακά that come to be (γίγνεται) in cities. Health as an existing condition (μετὰ ὑγιείας) contrasts with evils described through their coming-into-being (γίγνεται), one a state, the other a process with a discovered origin (γένεσιν).

elements.context: οὐ πόλιν … σκοποῦμεν μόνον ὅπως γίγνεται

new_signals.observation: πόλις appears four times in rapid succession at 372e as Socrates distinguishes the city they were examining (σκοποῦμεν) from a luxurious city (τρυφῶσαν πόλιν), then identifies the true city (ἀληθινὴ πόλις) and proposes examining the inflamed city (φλεγμαίνουσαν πόλιν). The concentration marks the moment the singular object of inquiry splits into two.

γίγνομαι appears first for how a city comes to be, then shifts to ἐμφύονται (grow in, are implanted) for how justice and injustice arise in cities, then returns twice for how evils come to be when war comes to be. The verb's recurrence traces coming-into-being from the city's generation through the implanting of justice and injustice to the genesis of evils.

elements.context: ἡ τότε ἱκανὴ τρέφειν τοὺς τότε

new_signals.observation: τότε appears twice in immediate succession, first modifying the land (ἡ τότε … χώρα), then modifying the people (τοὺς τότε), creating a doubling that marks both territory and population as belonging to a past moment of sufficiency.

elements.context: ἐν τῇ προτέρᾳ πόλει οὐκ ἐνῆν
ἐν δὲ ταύτῃ καὶ τούτου προσδεήσει

new_signals.observation: The earlier city (προτέρᾳ πόλει) did not contain swineherds because there was no need; in this one (ταύτῃ) there will be additional need (προσδεήσει) of them. The demonstrative contrast (ἐν τῇ … ἐν δὲ ταύτῃ) sets the two cities in immediate spatial-logical opposition.
